SCHOOL GARDEN · GARDEN THINGS

Garden Things

Age 2 YearsSubject Nature & TalkClass School GardenDuration 3–5 minutes

A garden is full of things with names: the tree at the gate, the watering can, the wheelbarrow, the bench where you sit. Twelve garden things, one big picture at a time.

Nothing to prepare and nothing to read. You say the name, your toddler points or wanders over — a moment on a card counts, and the real garden can wait for your next walk.

Start the Class ↓Start with the flower — the one they already know.
TODAY’S CLASS

How today’s class works.

Ten little steps, in order: a welcome from your teacher, all twelve garden things, two gentle games, a name-it-as-you-go walk, cards to print, a note from your teacher and one last check-in from you. Stop after any step — that is a complete class.

  1. 1 Teacher welcome
  2. 2 Meet the garden things
  3. 3 Find the thing
  4. 4 What is it for?
  5. 5 Around the garden
  6. 6 Take it off screen
  7. 7 Print the cards
  8. 8 Teacher note
  9. 9 Parent review
  10. 10 Class complete

LEARN · MEET THE GARDEN THINGS

Meet the garden things.

Twelve garden things, one at a time. Say the name clearly, and let your toddler point, wiggle or wander along.

Card 1 of 12
Or simply scroll: all 12 cards are below.
PLAY · FIND THE THING

Find the thing.

Three pictures, one question. You say the garden thing, your child taps it — a wrong tap simply means look together.

Find the tree.

Where is the watering can?

Find the wheelbarrow.

Can you find the rake?

Where is the garden bench?

PLAY · WHAT IS IT FOR?

What is it for?

A little clue about the job each thing does, then three pictures. Every guess is a good guess.

I water the plants. What am I?

I dig big holes. What am I?

I carry soil and plants. What am I?

You sit and rest on me. What am I?

I am a home for a little plant. What am I?

TOGETHER · AROUND THE GARDEN

Around the garden.

Where each thing lives and what it does — a little tour for your next walk outside.

  • Tree

    “Standing at the gate or in the park — bark to touch, leaves to peek at.”

  • Watering can

    “By the tap or the shed, ready for plant drink time.”

  • Fence

    “Around the edge — follow it all the way round the garden.”

  • Garden bench

    “In a sunny or shady spot — the best seat for a snack.”

  • Wheelbarrow

    “Tipped by the shed — one wheel, two handles, big jobs.”

  • Grass

    “Under your feet everywhere — bare toes love it in summer.”

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

A name-it-as-you-go garden walk.

Take the names outside — or to a park, a balcony or a window box if a garden is far away.

Try one today

  • Water a plant together — pss-pss with the watering can or a cup.
  • Touch the tree trunk on your walk and say tree, big tree.
  • Sit on a bench and name three things you can see from it.
  • Spot a fence, a wheelie bin, a gate — garden words live on every street.
  • Dig in a sandpit or a pot of soil with a spoon — your own little shovel.

Real tools are grown-up tools: shovels and rakes and hoses stay in grown-up hands. Watching, naming and your own spoon-digging is the toddler version — with a grown-up close the whole time.

A NOTE FROM THE PRINCIPAL

For the grown-ups.

Tool words are everyday words. Saying watering can while you water a plant is the whole lesson — and the tools themselves stay grown-up territory.

More from the Principal’s Office ↗

CLASS COMPLETE

Class complete!

From the tall tree to the bench where you rest — what a garden full of names. However many rounds you played, however long it took, that was the whole class — and stopping early is allowed too.

TIPS FOR PARENTS

Tips for Parents

Name the things you pass — tree, gate, bench. Everyday objects are the easiest words to practise.

Let them do the toddler version: water with a cup, dig with a spoon, push an invisible wheelbarrow.

Real tools stay in grown-up hands. Naming a shovel is plenty — touching it can wait for big-kid years.

Age ranges are a guide. Go at your child’s pace.
